maria: FYI pushed a tiny RSC+Astro hybrid quickstart that wires LlamaIndex for docs KV. noticed weirdness in SSR path where the KV cache doesn't rehydrate so embeddings regen on every server render. repro steps in the repo: https://git.company/repo/quick-rsc-astro jon: ugh, that's rough. do you see it on hosted or local dev only? sam: tagging @dev-bot to capture telemetry events for that thread :eyes: dev-bot: captured event stream for commit f3a2c1a — sent trace id trace-9fb3 to ops. maria: repro on both local and our dedicated env. local faster to iterate. happens when the page uses a Server Component that imports LlamaIndex loader and then the client calls embedsvia edge function — the server-side KV doesn't seem to persist across SSR reused renders. laura: can you paste the minimal server component? maybe it's an RSC lifecycle/streaming quirk. maria: sure — snippet below: ```jsx // app/search/page.server.jsx import { loadIndex } from 'llamaindex' export default async function Page() { const idx = await loadIndex('docs-kv') const results = await idx.query('colors') return
{results[0].text}
} ``` jon: and the KV init is in an edge-route? that mismatch can cause two different runtimes to own state. did you put the index init behind `if (typeof window === 'undefined')`? maria: no, we used the SDK default which tries to pick runtime. suspect parity issue: server runtime path uses `@redwood/inference-node` but edge client path uses `@redwood/inference-edge` via the SDK. maybe the index serialization formats differ. sam: that sounds like an SDK parity bug — node vs edge serialize the KV snapshot differently. we saw similar with quantized weights earlier. laura: quick check: are you seeing any auth retry spikes around the same time? if the client edge call is failing and falling back to a new index build, that would explain regen. maria: logs show a couple of 401->200 retries but mostly 200. here's the log snippet: ``` 2026-03-23T16:12:03Z INFO fetch-index docs-kv status=200 size=162kb 2026-03-23T16:12:04Z WARN auth refresh retry=1 code=401 2026-03-23T16:12:05Z INFO fetch-index docs-kv status=200 size=162kb ``` jon: hmm, the 401 flap could cause the server to fallback to a local cached build which doesn't persist to the same KV namespace. Could be a race between token rotation and index persist. sam: workaround idea: explicit config to pin runtime and storage adapter in the starter. e.g. `new LlamaIndex({ storage: new RedwoodKV({ namespace: 'docs-kv', backend: 'node' }) })` so both server and edge agree. maria: yeah adding explicit adapter fixed it in my quick patch. but we should make starter opinionated to avoid TOCTOU for new users. laura: agree — UX wise, this will be a major onboarding footgun. can we add a startup validation step in the template that warns when runtimes differ? jon: add a small dev-time check that compares `typeof process` and `navigator` usage and prints a warning in console and in test harness. PR sketch: add `scripts/validate-runtime.js` and run it in `postinstall`. sam: also add a small note in the README about auth token rotation for long-lived pages and recommend server-only index builds + client-side embedding calls. maria: I'll open a PR with the validator + README note + example config. cc @laura for review. laura: thanks — can you also include a tiny eval harness test that asserts index persists across a simulated SSR cycle? we can wire it into our CI quickcheck. maria: yep will add a jest e2e that spawns a headless render -> edge embed call -> assert no new index build (via trace id). jon: nice. marking this as low-sev DX but high-impact for starters. :white_check_mark: sam: once PR is in, we should backport the validator to other starters to avoid duplicate fallout. maria: PR in progress, will ping when ready. thanks all! :pray:
